name: actin-to-membrane-force-handshake
title: Coupler A · Actin→membrane force handshake
claim: OBSERVED (option B, magnitude-conserving): the coupler now sizes the osmotic offset so its integrated membrane force equals the actin contact force; force_residual ≈ 0 every step. CAVEAT: pressure-mediated effective-force handshake, not an independent per-vertex check (that is option A, blocked by a pymem3dg applied-force segfault — tracked).
decision_figure: actin force, membrane force, residual force, and residual impulse vs time (residual → 0), plus a histogram of transferred forces to flag numerical outliers
expected_pattern: residual force ≈ 0 throughout; transferred-force histogram has no heavy tails/outliers
question: In the closed-loop flexible composite, is the force the actin side reports at the interface equal-and-opposite to the force the membrane integrates on its receiving vertices (Newton's 3rd law on the coupling interface)?

purpose.question: In the closed-loop flexible composite, is the force the actin side reports at the interface equal-and-opposite to the force the membrane integrates on its receiving vertices (Newton's 3rd law on the coupling interface)?
purpose.mechanism: BrownianRatchetCoupler reads ReaDDy tip positions, computes per-contact forces using contact_threshold + force_constant, and applies them as osmotic_offset on Mem3DG. The same per-step force scalar must show up in both the actin-side contact_force observable and the membrane-side integrated impulse, up to numerical tolerance.

variants.name: weak-coupling
variants.description: Low force-to-displacement scale — small per-contact impulse to test 3rd-law balance at low signal.

variants.name: strong-coupling
variants.description: High force-to-displacement scale — stresses momentum bookkeeping at large impulses.

tests.name: newton-third-law-holds-on-interface
tests.question: Per-step (membrane integrated impulse + actin contact_force·dt) sums to within 5% of zero, sample-by-sample.

modified_processes: BrownianRatchetCoupler: instrument the force-publication path to expose per-contact force magnitudes for handshake verification.
model_change.notes: Tests that the force the ReaDDy side reports equals the force Mem3DG receives at the interface (Newton's 3rd law) within numerical tolerance.

simulation_set.name: handshake-flexible
simulation_set.description: Same rung-3 composite as flexible-mem3dg-boundary, run for handshake-direction-A verification.

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Is the actin→membrane coupling momentum-faithful (Newton's 3rd law) at the interface?
resolved_uncertainties: Under option B the coupler delivers a membrane pressure-force equal to the actin contact force; force_residual ~0 every step.
remaining_uncertainties: This is magnitude-conservation through the osmotic channel, NOT an independent per-vertex force exchange — option A (a genuine applied force in pymem3dg) is blocked by a binding segfault.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: residual~0 is a bookkeeping identity (offset sized as contact_force/area), not evidence the simulator conserves momentum locally.
evidence_against: an independent readback of the integrated applied force matching contact_force (option A) would be a true check.
discriminating_observables: net force on the closed vesicle

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Coupling transmits the contact-force MAGNITUDE as a global osmotic pressure; locality/momentum is unverified.

followup_study_proposals.title: Option A — apply a genuine local contact force in pymem3dg and read it back
